- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, expect overshoot or overconfidence; adjust downward by 2–5% for next period if recent price spike occurred.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model forecasts tend to underreact; increase forecast baseline by 1–3% to account for suppressed volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overcorrects downward; apply a 1–3% upward bias to offset lagged mean reversion.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.50), model forecasts are prone to underestimating volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast baseline for next 3–5 days.
- If official event count is high (≥20 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to overpredict price stability; reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per event to reflect event-induced noise.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is bearish and price has been trending upward, model often fails to recognize reversal; apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and model forecasts are rising, expect reversal; reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5 per day until sentiment stabilizes.
